ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r1.claim: Jurz describes land stripped by drought, locusts, or similar causes, left without vegetation; a barren year is called jarz, and a woman who eats much is jawz.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r1.anchor: سنة جرز وسنون أجراز لا مطر فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r2.claim: A poetic line about an old gluttonous woman illustrates jawz as voracious.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
إن العجوز خبة جروزا ... تأكل كل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r11.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r11.claim: Muqātil regards the opening through the verse ending juruzan and the verses about believers who do good deeds as Medinan exceptions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p133/r11.anchor: مقاتل: إلا من أولها إلى جرزا ومن قوله إن الذين آمنوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r14.claim: God will turn what adorned the earth, or everything on it, into barren soil; this urges detachment from the world and consoles the Prophet since its beauty will perish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r14.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى التزهيد في الدنيا والرغبة عنها وتسلية للرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī pictures the earth stripped of vegetation and life, its green beauty made a bare white surface.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r15.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ما عليها من هذه الزينة صعيدا جرزا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r16.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r16.claim: Mujāhid says ṣaʿīd is ground without plants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r16.anchor: مجاهد: الأرض التي لا نبات بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r17.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r17.claim: Al-Suddī defines ṣaʿīd as smooth, level ground; other views call it a road.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p140/r17.anchor: وقال السدي الأملس المستوي. وقيل: الطريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p141/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p141/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p141/r1.claim: A hadith warns against sitting on ṣuʿud, elevated or open paths.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r4.claim: The barren plain signifies the world's annihilation becoming manifest when true divine existence and the greater Resurrection appear.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p258/r4.anchor: كناية عن ظهور فناء ذلك بظهور الوجود الحقاني والقيامة الكبرى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r2.claim: God will turn the earth's adornment into barren white land, removing its beauty as animals die and vegetation dries.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p659/r2.anchor: بعد أن كانت خضراء معشبة ، في إزالة بهجته ، وإماطة حسنه

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.claim: Al-Kahf is late Makkan, although a minority consider its first eight verses Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.anchor: is a late Makkan sūrah, although a minority hold

TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.claim: God is better in reward and outcome because His reality endures, while worldly adornments fade; since people need something to rely on for their affairs, their Lord is better.
TABATABAI:18:42-44#2/r4.anchor: لأنه سبحانه هو الحق الثابت الذي لا يفنى ولا يزول

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains the coming barren plain as ruin.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r2.anchor: {صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8] والجرز هاهنا: الخراب في تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r3.claim: Qatāda defines the barren ground as land without trees or buildings.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: التي ليس فيها شجر ولا بناء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r4.speaker: ابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r4.claim: Ibn Mujāhid's father says the plain will be bare and level.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r4.anchor: وقال ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: بلقعا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r5.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r5.claim: Yaḥyā connects this barren ground to the dry, plantless earth in another verse, from which God brings out crops by water.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p172/r5.anchor: قال يحيى: وهي في موضع آخر حيث قالوا: {أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز} [السجدة: 27] اليابسة التي ليس فيها نبات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word “juruza” means barren land; the world’s attractions are temporary and God will destroy them, as discussed further in verses 46–48.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word ﺟﺮز refers to barren land

BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r10.claim: When the world's life ends, God will turn everything on earth into bare, barren ground without vegetation; al-Kashifi warns against attachment to fleeting adornment.
BURSEVI:v5p167#2/r10.anchor: ترابا {جرزا} لا نبات فيه وسنة جرز

BURSEVI:v5p168#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p168#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p168#2/r1.claim: The closing verses urge detachment from the fleeting world and prayer to be among those who turn wholly toward God.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.claim: Muqatil says the surah is Meccan except its opening through “barren ground” (18:8) and the passage beginning “Indeed, those who believe” through the end.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هي مكية إلا أولها إلى ( جرزا ) وقوله تعالى : ( إن الذين آمنوا ) إلى آخرها فمدني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r1.claim: The phrase refers to everything placed on earth, while some exegetes take it more broadly than the adornment mentioned earlier; the unexpressed pronoun intensifies the statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r1.anchor: وجوز غير واحد أن يكون هذا أعم مما جعل زينة ولذا لم يؤت بالضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r2.claim: Here jaʿl means transforming what is on earth into barren soil.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r2.anchor: والجعل هنا بمعنى التصيير أي مصيرون ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r3.claim: Juruz means land with no vegetation; al-Alusi treats this as the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r3.anchor: لا نبات فيه قاله قتادة وقال الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r4.speaker: الراغب وأبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface; Abu Ubayda calls it level ground.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r4.anchor: الراغب : الصعيد وجه الأرض وقال أبو عبيدة هو المستوى من الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r5.claim: Ṣaʿīd means level ground; this is also transmitted from al-Suddi.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة هو المستوى من الأرض وروي ذلك عن السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r6.claim: Ṣaʿīd is a road without vegetation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r7.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r7.claim: He transmits that juruz means ruined, but al-Alusi says this is not the genuine lexical meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم أن الجزر الخراب والظاهر أنه ليس معنى حقيقا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r8.claim: Lexical usage describes barren land as vegetation lost through drought or locusts, and years without rain as juruz years.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r8.anchor: يقال جزرت الأرض فهي مجروزة إذا ذهب نباتها بقحط أو جراد وأرضون أجراز لا نبات فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r9.claim: The image is plain soil where spectators once marveled at the earth's beauty and enjoyed seeing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r9.anchor: والمراد ما على الأرض ترابا ساذجا بعد ما كان يتعجب من بهجته النظار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r10.claim: Taken literally over every component, the transformation entails created elements changing into earth, which is possible because elements already change into one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r10.anchor: وذلك إنما يكون بقلب سائر عناصر المواليد إلى عنصر التراب ولا استحالة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r11.claim: An ordinary idiom can mean that a person's body decayed until only earth remained; people would not imagine elemental conversion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r11.anchor: فإن الناس يقولون صار فلان ترابا إذا اضمحل جسده ولم يبق منه أثر إلا التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r12.claim: Some philosophers held that elemental forms persist within composite bodies; al-Alusi adds that this account is scarcely heard from the early Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r12.anchor: وكذا زعم محققي الفلاسفة بقاء صور العناصر في المواليد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r13.claim: Al-Alusi says elemental conversion is scarcely heard from the early Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r13.anchor: وهذا الحديث لا تكاد تسمعه عن السلف الصالح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r14.claim: One coherence reading makes 18:7 explain the concern expressed earlier and 18:8 complete it: earthly beauty is a test, soon removed before recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r14.anchor: قوله تعالى ( إنا جعلنا ) الخ تعليل لما في لعل من معنى الإشفاق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r15.claim: Another reading says the passage consoles Muhammad: do not grieve over denial, since God will soon avenge him; the opening also says he warns but cannot create faith in them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r15.anchor: لا تحزن بما عاينت من القوم من تكذيب ما أنزلنا عليك من الكتاب فإنا قد جعلنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r16.claim: A further proposed link urges Muhammad to keep calling people despite their rebellion, as God sustains them; the second clause would discourage attachment to worldly adornment, but al-Alusi finds this link strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p207#2/r16.anchor: وهذا تضمن إرشاده إلى التخلق ببعض أخلاقه تعالى كأنه قيل إني خلقت الأرض وزينتها ابتلاء للخلق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r2.claim: Ṣaʿīd means the face of the earth; another gloss calls it soil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r2.anchor: فالصعيد وجه الأرض. وقيل: هو التراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r3.claim: Juruz is dry, smooth, barren ground without growth; the root describes land whose plants have been eaten away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p144#2/r3.anchor: "جرزا" يابسا أملس لا ينبت شيئا. يقال: جرزت الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r1.claim: The verse discourages attachment to worldly adornment by promising to turn it into earth and leave the surface smooth and barren.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r1.anchor: والمعنى إنا لنعيد ما عليها من الزينة ترابا مستويا بالأرض ونجعله كصعيد أملس لا نبات فيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r2.claim: Jarz is land whose vegetation has been cut away, from the verb meaning to cut.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:8/r2.anchor: والجرز الأرض التي قطع نباتها. مأخوذ من الجرز وهو القطع

QASHANI:18:7-9/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:7-9/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:7-9/r3.claim: God can reduce the world's adornment to a barren plain by divine manifestation and the annihilation of its qualities, through true or natural death, without injustice or loss.
QASHANI:18:7-9/r3.anchor: ثم نفنيها ولا حيف ولا نقص

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r8.claim: God removes the world's adornment by stripping away greenery, then subjecting it to sun and wind until it returns to bare, dry soil that naturally grows nothing.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r8.anchor: نهلك تلك الزينة بإزالة اخضرارها فيزول المانع من استيلاء التراب عليها ثم نسلط عليها الشموس والرياح

BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r9.claim: The same affliction may befall animals, human or otherwise; recurring plant restoration by rain is an evident resurrection proof, omitted for readers of insight.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p446/r9.anchor: وكذا نفعل بمن سبب تسليط البلاء عليه من الحيوان آدميا كان أو غيره سواء . ولما كان من المشاهد

DURR-FULL:v5p361/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r1.claim: The barren ground will destroy and make perish everything upon it.
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} قال: يهلك كل شيء عليها ويبيد

DURR-FULL:v5p361/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r2.claim: Saʿīd is soil; juruz describes land without vegetation or growth.
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {صعيدا جرزا} قال: الصعيد التراب

DURR-FULL:v5p361/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p361/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {جرزا} قال: يعني بالجزر الخراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r1.claim: The Prophet called the surah al-Kahf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r1.anchor: سماها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سورة الكهف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r2.claim: Muslim and Abū Dāwūd report from Abū al-Dardāʾ that memorizing ten opening verses protects from the Dajjāl; Muslim also says ten final verses. Al-Tirmidhī reports three opening verses and grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r2.anchor: من حفظ عشر آيات من أول سورة الكهف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r3.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib's Bukhārī report names the surah: a cloud covered a man reciting it by a tethered horse, which became restless; the Prophet identified it as tranquility descending with the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r3.anchor: وكذلك وردت تسميتها عن البراء بن عازب في ( صحيح البخاري )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r4.claim: A report by Ibn Mardawayh says the Prophet called it Sūrat Aṣḥāb al-Kahf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r4.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه ابن مردويه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سماها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports consensus that the surah is Meccan. Farqad's report makes 18:1-8 Medinan, but he prefers the Meccan account; proposed Medinan passages at 18:28-29 and 18:107-end are weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r5.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق كما حكاه ابن عطية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r6.claim: The surah followed al-Ghāshiyah and preceded al-Shūrā; Jābir ibn Zayd ranks it sixty-eighth in revelation order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r6.anchor: نزلت بعد سورة الغاشية وقبل سورة الشورى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r7.claim: Its virtue reports vary in strength, with those already cited the soundest; another report says the whole surah descended at once with seventy thousand angels, omitted by al-Suyūṭī from al-Itqān.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r7.anchor: وهي من السور التي نزلت جملة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r8.claim: Verse counts differ: Medina and Mecca count 105, Syria 106, Basra 111, and Kufa 110 because they split some verses differently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p241/r8.anchor: عدت آيها في عدد قراء المدينة ومكة مائة وخمسا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.claim: The sentence beginning with inna explains the consolation in verse 6 and connects to the warning of severe punishment in verse 2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r2.anchor: وموقع ( إن ) في صدر هذه الجملة موقع التعليل للتسلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.claim: The reversal between earthly life and death recalls God's power over opposites and teaches people not to trust strength, but to prepare for changing states and judge themselves by virtue and good outcomes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r3.anchor: ويحصل من ذلك تذكير بعضهم قدرة الله تعالى ، وخاصة ما كان منها إيجادا للأشياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.claim: Earth is the closest sign to human perception and reflection, as other verses likewise direct people to observe the earth and creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r4.anchor: وأوثر الاستدلال بحال الأرض التي عليها الناس لأنها أقرب إلى حسهم وتعقلهم ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r5.claim: The wording compresses several purposes: gratitude for a world fitted with beautiful adornments and recognition of God's artistry, as in other descriptions of worldly beauty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p256#2/r5.anchor: الامتنان على الناس والتذكير ببديع صنع الله إذ وضع هذا العالم على أتقن مثال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r1.claim: The clause completes the lesson by confirming the world's eventual end; ja'ilun is an active participle used for the future, when all earthly life becomes dry, bare soil.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p258/r2.claim: Sa'id means soil, while juruz means barren and bare; the meaning of sa'id is revisited at verse 40.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r1.speaker: جميع المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r1.claim: All commentators say the sūra is Meccan; a minority says its opening through 18:8 came in Medina, but the author prefers the first view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول جميع المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r2.claim: The sūra is among the Qur'an's most excellent chapters.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r3.claim: Reports attribute great merit: Friday recitation brings forgiveness to the next Friday plus three days; another promises light and protection from the grave's trial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494/r3.anchor: من قرأ بها يوم الجمعة غفر له ما بينه وبين الجمعة الأخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r7.claim: Earth's adornment will become barren dust without plants; jurz is empty land, happening region by region now and to all earth at resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r7.anchor: أي يرجع كل ذلك ترابا غير متزين بنبات ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r8.claim: Jarazat describes land stripped of vegetation by drought, locusts, or similar causes; arḍūn ajrāz means barren lands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r8.anchor: يقال: جرزت الأرض بقحط أو جراد أو نحوه إذا ذهب نباتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines jurz as land that does not grow; the author corrects this to land that has not grown.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497/r9.anchor: قال الزجاج: والجرز الأرض التي لا تنبت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497#2/r1.claim: Ṣaʿīd can mean the earth's surface, soil specifically, wholesome earth, or ground raised above a lower area.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p497#2/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وإنما ينبغي أن يقول: التي لم تنبت، و «الصعيد» وجه الأرض

SULAMI:v1p402/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p402/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p402/r1.claim: The cosmos is held in God's grasp and is mere dust beside His power.
SULAMI:v1p402/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : الكون في قبضة الحق وهو هباء في جنب القدرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines ṣaʿīd as a path without vegetation; Ibn al-Anbari reports the lexicographers’ gloss of soil or the earth’s surface.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج الصعيد الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه وقال ابن الأنباري قال اللغويون الصعيد التراب ووجه الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r2.claim: Al-Farra describes dialectal differences in the vowel patterns used for jarz across Hijaz, Asad, and Tamim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r2.anchor: فأما الجرز فقال الفراء أهل الحجاز يقولون أرض جرز وجرز وأسد تقول جرز وجرز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda defines ṣaʿīd jarz as coarse barren ground; a year called jarz is drought-struck with little rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r3.anchor: الصعيد الجرز الغليظ الذي لا ينبت شيئا ويقال للسنة المجدبة جرز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r4.claim: A poetic line attests the phrase al-sinūn al-ajraz, years of barrenness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says jarz is land where nothing grows, as though it consumes vegetation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r5.anchor: الأرض التي لا ينبت فيها شيء كأنها تأكل النبت أكلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reports that jarz is land left without vegetation, consuming or burning every plant there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r6.anchor: الأرض التي لا يبقى بها نبات تحرق كل نبات يكون بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r7.claim: Exegetes say this will happen at resurrection, when God makes the earth level, without plant or water.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p106/r7.anchor: وهذا يكون يوم القيامة يجعل الله الأرض مستوية لا نبات فيها ولا ماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r8.claim: After its adornment, the world will be destroyed and everything on it will perish, becoming barren ground that neither grows nor benefits anyone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r8.anchor: أي: وإنا لمصيروها بعد الزينة إلى الخراب والدمار، فنجعل كل شيء عليها هالكا {صعيدا جرزا} : لا ينبت ولا ينتفع به،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r9.claim: Al-Awfi reports Ibn Abbas’s gloss that everything on earth will be destroyed and perish.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r9.anchor: كما قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} يقول: يهلك كل شيء عليها ويبيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r10.claim: Mujahid explains the barren ground as a desolate, level place.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r11.claim: Qatada defines the ground as having no tree or vegetation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: الصعيد: الأرض التي ليس فيها شجر ولا نبات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r12.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd says the ground will contain nothing and connects the image to 32:27, where water is driven to barren land to produce crops.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الصعيد: الأرض التي ليس فيها شيء، ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى: {أولم يروا أنا نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the earth and everything on it will perish and return to God, so the Prophet should not grieve over what he hears or sees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} يعني الأرض، إن ما عليها لفان وبائد، وإن المرجع لإلى الله (8) فلا تأس ولا يحزنك ما تسمع وترى.

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r6.claim: Jarz describes dry barren land without vegetation and is also used of drought-stricken years.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r6.anchor: والجرز: اليابس الذي لا نبت فيه، يقال: جرزت الأرض فهي مجروزة، وسنة جرز،

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r7.claim: Abu Muslim derives jarz from cutting, as in a sharp sword or a person who eats everything.
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r7.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الجرز: القطع، يقال: سيف جراز إذا كان قاطعا ماضيا،

JISHUMI:v6p4344/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4344/r9.claim: صعيدا is accusative as the object of جاعلون.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r4.claim: God will ruin the earth after its flourishing, turning its contents into barren ground.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r4.anchor: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا يعني مخربون الأرض بعد عمارتها بجعل ما عليها صعيدا؛

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r5.claim: One gloss calls the transformed earth dry and without vegetation.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r6.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r6.claim: Another gloss calls it a barren plain, attributed to Mujahid.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r7.claim: A further explanation takes it as harvested and cut down.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r7.anchor: وقيل: أرضا محصودا [كل ما] كان عليها؟ أي: قطع.

JISHUMI:v6p4345/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r11.claim: The earth becomes barren when moral responsibility ends, bodies perish, and the signs of the Hour occur.
JISHUMI:v6p4345/r11.anchor: وتدل على أنها تصير بلقعا لا نبت عليها، وأنها كذلك عند انقطاع التكليف وفناء الأجسام، وثبوت أشراط الساعة.

FARRA:v2p134/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p134/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p134/r3.claim: صعيد is soil; جُرُز describes barren land without vegetation, and the land is called مجروزة after grazing animals or locusts consume its growth.
FARRA:v2p134/r3.anchor: وقوله: صعيدا [8] الصعيد التراب. والجرز: أن تكون الأرض لا نبات فيها.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r11.speaker: الأخفش ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r11.claim: Saʿīd means a level stretch of land.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r11.anchor: أحدها : الأرض المستوية , قاله الأخفش ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r12.claim: Saʿīd means the face of the earth, because it rises or projects.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r12.anchor: الثاني : هو وجه الأرض لصعوده , قاله ابن قتيبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r13.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r13.anchor: الثالث : أنه التراب , قاله أبان بن تغلب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r14.claim: Juruz means barren and empty land.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r16.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r16.anchor: الثالث : محصورة , وهو قول ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r17.claim: Juruz means dry earth with no plants or crops; a rajaz verse uses the cognate for what the years have stripped bare.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p285/r17.anchor: الرابع : أنها اليابسة التي لا نبات بها ولا زرع قال الراجز :

MUJAHID:v1p373#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p373#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p373#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses ṣaʿīdan juruzan as a barren, bare plain.
MUJAHID:v1p373#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ صعيدا جرزا ﴾ قال يعني بلقعا

MUQATIL:18:6-8/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r3.claim: In the afterlife everything on earth becomes smooth, level, and bare of mountains and plants, as at first creation.
MUQATIL:18:6-8/r3.anchor: { وإنا لجاعلون } في الآخرة، { ما عليها } ، يعني ما على الأرض من شىء، { صعيدا } ، يعني مستويا، { جرزا }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#3/r1.claim: The adornments will become smooth, dry, barren ground with no vegetation; after its flourishing, the earth is ruined as living beings die and plants dry up.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p4#3/r1.anchor: يابسا لا نبات فيها بعد أن كانت خضراء معشبة والمعنى نعيدها بعد عمارتها خرابا باماتة الحيوان وتجفيف النبات والأشجار

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r12.speaker: ابن هشام
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r12.claim: Ibn Hisham defines saeid as the earth's surface and cites Dhu al-Rumma's line as poetic usage; it also means a road, as in a hadith.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r12.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الصعيد وجه الأرض، وجمعه صعد.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#2/r1.claim: The hadith warning against sitting on saeid refers to roads, and jarz is barren land that produces nothing, including a drought-stricken year.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#2/r1.anchor:
إياكم والقعود على الصعدات "
يريد الطرق. والجرز: الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r1.speaker: أبو سهل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r1.claim: Abu Sahl says the earth will become soil without vegetation, as though its plants were cut away; jarz is related to cutting.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r1.anchor: وقال أبو سهل: ترابا لا نبات به كأنه قطع نباته. والجرز: القطع

QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r2.claim: A barren earth has no vegetation or structures, as if all were removed; this refers to resurrection, when the ground is level and offers no shelter.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r2.anchor: والأرض الجرز التي لا نبات فيها ولا شيء من عمارة وغيرها كأنه قطع وأزيل

QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas gives the lexical definition of jarz as land with no plants.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r3.anchor: النحاس: والجرز في اللغة الأرض التي لا نبات بها.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r4.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r4.claim: Al-Kisai says the land is jaraz when people consume every plant and crop; the derived forms describe depleted land.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:8/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي: يقال جرزت الأرض تجرز، وجرزها القوم يجرزونها إذا أكلوا كل ما جاء فيها

MAJAZ:v1p393/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p393/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p393/r4.claim: صعيدا means level ground or the surface of the earth.

MAJAZ:v1p393/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p393/r5.claim: جرزا means barren, growing nothing; أرضون أجراز and جرز years are dry, low-rain, infertile land and years, as Dhū al-Rumma’s lines illustrate.
MAJAZ:v1p393/r5.anchor: «جرزا» (8) أي غلظا لا ينبت شيئا والجميع أرضون أجراز، ويقال للسنة المجدبة: جرز وسنون أجراز

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r5.claim: Earth is adorned for trial, not perpetual enjoyment; its contents will be destroyed before recompense, and other verses show the earth itself will also be transformed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r5.anchor: لا لأجل أن يبقى الإنسان فيها متنعما أبدا لأنه يزهد فيها

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda defines al-sa'id as level ground.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الصعيد المستوي من الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r7.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines al-sa'id as a path without vegetation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r8.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r8.claim: Al-Farra defines al-juruz as land with no vegetation, stripped bare by grazing; the root also describes a voracious woman and a destructive sword.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r8.anchor: فقال الفراء : الجرز الأرض التي لا نبات عليها

RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r9.claim: The same barren-land expression appears in the verse about water being driven to the barren plain.
RAZI-FULL:v21p68/r9.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { نسوق الماء إلى الارض الجرز }

STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.claim: Earth’s adornment includes its plants, animals, gold, and metals; al-Rāzī considers humanity its noblest creature.
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r1.anchor: The earth is “adorned” by the various phenomena found upon it or in it, including its flora and fauna and its precious gold and metals

STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.speaker: Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazzālī
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.claim: Earthly adornment tests whether people maintain detachment and asceticism toward the world.
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r2.anchor: the “adornment” of the earth is a means by which God tries human beings with regard to their ability to maintain an attitude of detachment and asceticism toward the world

STUDYQURAN:18:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r3.claim: The barren plain means earthly adornments will not last but will end and return to God.
STUDYQURAN:18:7/r3.anchor: none of its adornments will endure forever, but will come to end and return to God (IK)

NAHHAS:v2p447/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p447/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p447/r12.claim: The adornment on earth will all be made a barren plain.
NAHHAS:v2p447/r12.anchor: فالحسن العمل الذي يزهد في الزينة ثم أعلم الله عز وجل أنه مبيد ذلك كله

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says everything on earth will perish and disappear.
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8] يقول: يهلك كل شيء عليها ويبيد

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses ṣaʿīd juruz as an empty, barren plain.

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r3.claim: Qatada defines ṣaʿīd as land without trees or vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8] والصعيد: الأرض التي ليس فيها شجر ولا نبات

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says all on earth will perish and return to God, so Muhammad should not grieve over what he sees and hears there.
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8] يعني: الأرض إن ما عليها لفان وبائد

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says juruz is land with nothing useful on it and ṣaʿīd is flat ground; he links it to the land that produces crops when water is driven to it.
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {صعيدا جرزا} [الكهف: 8] قال: الجرز: الأرض التي ليس فيها شيء

TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r6.claim: The root جرز describes barren land stripped by locusts or livestock, empty land and drought years; the cited rajaz line uses الأجراز for such years.
TAB-FULL:v15p153#2/r6.anchor: ويقال للسنة المجدبة: جرز، وسنون أجراز لجدوبها ويبسها وقلة أمطارها

TABATABAI:18:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.claim: The sūrah may have been revealed to present three unusual narratives found nowhere else in the Qurʾān—the Companions of the Cave, Moses and his companion, and Dhū al-Qarnayn—and derive lessons against associating partners and for piety.
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.anchor: ذكر القصص الثلاث العجيبة التي لم تذكر في القرآن الكريم إلا في هذه السورة

TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.claim: Earth's adornments are attractive goods, children, status, and other attachments; God uses them to draw lofty human souls into earthly life for a test, then removes their beauty and attachments when the term ends, leaving people alone for judgment.
TABATABAI:18:6-7/r3.anchor: فكان ما على الأرض وهو جميل عندهم محبوب في أنفسهم زينة للأرض وحليه تتحلى بها لكونه عليها

TABATABAI:18:8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:8/r1.claim: The worldly scene is a divinely imposed trial, so the Prophet should not grieve over people absorbed in its pleasures; they cannot defeat God's will, and only deeds endure.
TABATABAI:18:8/r1.anchor: فمحصل معنى الآية لا تتحرج ولا تأسف عليهم إذا عرضوا عن دعوتك بالإنذار والتبشير

TABATABAI:18:8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:8/r2.claim: The barren plain is a metaphor for severing human attachment to earthly possessions and adornments when their trial ends.
TABATABAI:18:8/r2.anchor: والمراد به قطع رابطة التعلق بين الإنسان وبين أمتعة الحياة الدنيا مما على الأرض

TABATABAI:18:8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:18:8/r3.claim: An alternative takes the image literally: the earth's adornment will become level dust, smooth and barren of growth or anything attractive.
TABATABAI:18:8/r3.anchor: المراد به حقيقة معنى الصعيد الجرز، والمعنى أنا سنعيد ما على الأرض من زينة

TABATABAI:18:8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:8/r4.claim: The wording ما عليها replaces an expected pronoun, perhaps to stress that the adornment lies upon the earth.
TABATABAI:18:8/r4.anchor: من قبيل وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر وكان من طبع الكلام أن يقال وإنا لجاعلوه

TABATABAI:18:8#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:8#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:18:8#2/r1.claim: In al-Qummī's report through Abū al-Jārūd, al-Bāqir explains ṣaʿīdan juruzan as land with no vegetation.
TABATABAI:18:8#2/r1.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { صعيدا جرزا } قال لا نبات فيها

TABRISI:18:7-8/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:7-8/r8.claim: God will ruin the inhabited earth and leave its surface level, dry, and without vegetation.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r8.anchor: وإنا مخربون الأرض بعد عمارتها وجاعلون ما عليها مستويا من الأرض

TABRISI:18:7-8/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:7-8/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:18:7-8/r9.claim: The barren surface may be understood as open, desolate plains.
TABRISI:18:7-8/r9.anchor: وقيل بلاقع عن مجاهد وفي قوله أيهم أحسن

THALABI:v6p144#4/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p144#4/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p144#4/r8.claim: God will make the earth level, barren, dry, smooth, and unable to grow anything.
THALABI:v6p144#4/r8.anchor: وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا: مستويا جرزا: يابسا أملس لا تنبت شيئا.

THALABI:v6p178/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p178/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p178/r1.claim: The criminals are polytheists who expect to enter the Fire; other glosses say rush into or descend into it. Al-Aʿmash reads ‘encounter it.’
THALABI:v6p178/r1.anchor: ورأى المجرمون: المشركون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها: داخلوها. وقال مجاهد:

THALABI:v6p178/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p178/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي
THALABI:v6p178/r2.claim: A disbeliever sees Hell and thinks he will enter it from a distance of forty years’ travel.
THALABI:v6p178/r2.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.claim: God will destroy all the earth's adornments, as the next verse says.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p528#2/r7.anchor: ثم أعلم جل وعز أنه [مبيد] (¬3) ومفن ذلك كله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r5.claim: The earth will become a barren plain without vegetation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:6-9/r5.anchor: { وإنا لجاعلون ما عليها صعيدا جرزا } بلاقع ليس فيها نبات.

ELMALILI:18:7-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r2.claim: Today's dazzling adornments will soon become dust and ruin; true good action serves their everlasting Creator rather than clinging to temporary beauty.
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r2.anchor: Bugün gözler kamaştıran o ziynetler, yarın bakarsın dünden yokmuş gibi harâb ü türâb olup gidecek.

ELMALILI:18:7-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r3.claim: One should not waste time grieving over what will perish, but strive for the best deeds in this testing ground.
ELMALILI:18:7-8/r3.anchor: o helâk olacaklara esef ile üzülmemeli, vakit geçirmemeli de bu imtihan meydanında en güzel amele çalışmalıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r3.claim: Worldly blessings are temporary: God will turn earthly beauty into debris and make the world a dry, empty desert, warning people not to become attached to it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r3.anchor: yeryüzündeki güzellikleri bir gün çerçöp haline getirip yok edeceğini, dünyayı insansız, hayvansız, ağaçsız, bitkisiz ve kupkuru bir çöl haline getireceğini bildirmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r4.claim: Nothing in this world lasts; only God endures, and the world will be transformed at the Resurrection as described in Ibrahim 14:48 and Rahman 55:26–27.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:6/r4.anchor: Dünyada sürekli olan hiçbir şey yoktur; kıyamet gününde dünya da değişecektir; kalıcı olan yalnız Allah’tır.

SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r1.claim: Ṣaʿīdan is the second object because jaʿalnā here can only mean transformation or making something into something else.
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r1.anchor: مفعول ثان، لأن الجعل هنا تصيير ليس إلا

SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r2.claim: Ṣaʿīd means soil, and juruz describes land without vegetation; a dry year has no rain and barren land has no plants.
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r2.anchor: والصعيد. التراب: والجرز: الذي لا نبات به. يقال: سنة جزر

SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r3.claim: Jarazat describes vegetation disappearing through drought or locusts; jaraza al-arḍ al-jarādu means locusts ate everything in it. Jarrūz can mean a gluttonous woman, as the cited comic line illustrates.
SAMIN-DURR:18:8/r3.anchor: وجرزت الأرض: إذا ذهب نباتها بقحط أو جراد وجرز الأرض الجراد: أكل

ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r3.claim: الصعيد is a path without vegetation; الجرز is land that grows nothing, as if it consumes plants, and its plural is أجراز.
ZAJJAJ:v3p269/r3.anchor: والصعيد الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه، والجرز الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n6/r1.claim: Asad's bracketed interpolation supplies the implied link between the preceding verses and the long passage that follows.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n6/r1.anchor: This interpolation establishes the elliptically implied connection between the long passage that follows and the preceding two verses.

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r1.claim: The Cave story is not more wondrous than other Qur'anic messages because its parable fits the Qur'an's ethical teaching.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r1.anchor: the allegory or parable based on this story is entirely in tune with the ethical doctrine propounded in the Qur'an as a whole

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r2.speaker: most commentators
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r2.claim: Most commentators place the story in early Christian history, linking it to Decius's third-century persecution and youths from Ephesus who slept for centuries.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r2.anchor: most of the commentators incline to the view that it relates to a phase in early Christian history - namely, the persecution of the Christians by Emperor Decius in the third century

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r3.speaker: most classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r3.claim: Most classical commentators rely on the Christian legend of the youths and their miraculous sleep to interpret the Qur'anic account.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r3.anchor: the majority of the classical commentators rely on this Christian legend

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r4.claim: Asad argues that the Christian telling developed from a much older oral tradition with pre-Christian Jewish sources.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r4.anchor: the Christian formulation of this theme is a later development of a much older oral tradition

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r5.speaker: Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir argues that the youths lived before the Christian era, since Jewish rabbis would not preserve a story of Christians after severing friendly relations with them.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r5.anchor: Ibn Kathir remarks in his commentary on verse 13 of this surah

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r6.claim: Asad proposes that the story's fundamentals allegorize the Essene movement, especially the secluded Qumran community; he notes Jesus may have belonged to the Essenes.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r6.anchor: we have before us a striking allegory relating to a movement which played an important role in Jewish religious history

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r7.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r7.speaker: Ibn 'Abbas
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r7.claim: Ibn 'Abbas and early authorities equate ar-raqim with marqum, something written, and with kitab, scripture.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r7.anchor: some of the earliest authorities - and particularly Ibn 'Abbas - regarded this expression as synonymous with marqum

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r8.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r8.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r8.claim: Razi says Arabic rhetoricians and philologists agree that ar-raqim means al-kitab, a writ or scripture.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r8.anchor: Razi adds that "all rhetoricians and Arabic philologists assert that ar-raqim signifies

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r9.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r9.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r9.claim: Qumran's scriptural study, copying, preservation, seclusion, and reputation for piety likely inspired the cave-sleep allegory.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r9.anchor: members of the Qumran community - the strictest group among the Essenes - devoted themselves entirely to the study, the copying and the preservation of the sacred scriptures

ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r10.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r10.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r10.claim: Whatever its origin, the Qur'an uses the story as a parable of resurrection and of faith-driven withdrawal from a wicked world, rewarded by spiritual awakening beyond time and death.
ASAD-NOTES:18:7#n7/r10.anchor: the fact remains that it is used in the Qur'an in a purely parabolic sense

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Like the previous sūrah, al-Kahf was revealed in the late Makkan conflict, as Quraysh sought to erase the Qur’ānic mission while Jews and Christians backed them indirectly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Like the previous sūrah, this sūrah was also revealed in that part of the Makkan period when the conflict between good and evil of the Prophet’s preaching mission had entered its final phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh are warned not to let worldly success lead them to reject an obvious truth, since God’s punishment is near if they persist in arrogance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Quryash are warned that in the wake of their worldly successes they should not try to arrogantly deny an obvious reality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet and companions are urged to patience and steadfastness, with hints of migration and glad tidings of coming victories granted by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) and his companions are urged to be patient and steadfast. Certain subtle indications are made of the upcoming phases of migration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Where the previous sūrah exposed Jews, al-Kahf and Maryam expose Christians; Quraysh risk losing the great opportunity God offers if they follow baseless opponents in rejecting it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Just as in the previous sūrah, S ūrah Banī Isrā’īl, the Jews are exposed, in this sūrah and in the next one – S ūrah Maryam – the Christians are exposed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet’s task is to warn and give glad tidings; unbelief among rebels reflects neither a defect in the Book nor a shortcoming in his preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is urged to be patient since his only responsibility is to warn and give glad tidings to his nation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People’s blindness comes from infatuation with worldly lures; the Prophet should not fret, because the world’s false ornament will be exposed and they will regret their conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The reason for this is that these people have become blind in their infatuation with the lures of this world.

BURHAN:v4p130/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.claim: Examples make the source and destination of transformation explicit; in “day a livelihood,” maʿāsh may mean a time noun or a verbal noun meaning livelihood.
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.anchor: في قوله ﴿ وجعلنا النهار معاشا ﴾ 15 اسم زمان

BURHAN:v2p140/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p140/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p140/r1.claim: A report says reciting the opening verses of al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal; the author says this means reciting them with knowledge and understanding.
BURHAN:v2p140/r1.anchor: من قرأ الآيات من أول سورة الكهف عصمه الله من فتنة الدحال يريد والله أعلم من قرأها بعلم ومعرفة

ITQAN:v1p49/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.claim: The listed exceptions in al-Kahf are its opening through 'barren ground', the command to keep patient company, and 'those who believe' through the sūra's end.
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.anchor: الكهف استثني من أولها إلى ﴿ جرزا ﴾ وقوله ﴿ واصبر نفسك ﴾ الآية

ITQAN:v4p377/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p377/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p377/r19.claim: Al-Jurz is the name of a land.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1007/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1007/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1007/r1.claim: The ornament belongs to the earth and what grows on it; flowers and other beauty delight viewers, as God's adornment of the sky does.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1007/r1.anchor: فالزينة هي للأرض والله تعالى قال (حَتَّىَ إِذَا أَخَذَتِ

IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r12.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r12.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r12.claim: Everything on earth will perish, and people return to God for recompense according to their deeds; therefore Muhammad should not grieve over what he sees.
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r12.anchor: أي الأرض، وإن ما عليها لفان وزائل، وإن المرجع إلي، فأجزي كلا بعمله
